one_month_reasoning: Dycom has no earnings inside 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. Its fiscal Q3 ends 2026-10-31 (guide: revenue $1.90-1.98B, adj. EBITDA $281-302M, adj. EPS $4.33-4.79) and is normally reported in late November, after the window. Inside the window are value-chain read-throughs only. (1) Carrier Q3 reports (AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, late Oct) come right after the Oct 9 SpaceX-Grain 800 MHz deal (~$8B per WSJ), which sent T-Mobile, Verizon and AT&T down 5.5-7.4% premarket and tower REITs up 6.7-8.3%. The read-through to DY is mixed: pressure on carrier capex budgets versus more terrestrial infrastructure. Verizon was already guiding 2026 capex down $0.5-1bn and AT&T up. (2) MasTec and Quanta Q3 (late Oct/early Nov): is MasTec Communications stable after Q2's -170bp margin? (3) Corning and hyperscaler Q3 capex updates (late Oct). Each can move DY a few percent, none is decisive, and the sector shock on Oct 9 is already in the $269.23 close. Momentum (new 52-week low) and oversold valuation (14.6x forward) pull opposite ways. Net: symmetric lognormal centred on $269.23 with monthly sigma 14.9% (52%/3.5), no directional tilt.

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x calendar-weighted NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ($21.33 = 0.31 x FY28E $19.95 + 0.69 x FY29E $21.95) = $341 (60%) and 10.5x FY28E adj. EBITDA $1.20B less $2.53B lease-inclusive horizon net debt over 30.16M shares = $334 (40%). Blended: 0.6 x 341 + 0.4 x 334 = $338.

inputs_detail.derivation: Communications was $1,608.4M of $2,005.9M Q2 revenue (80.2%, src 1) and DY now guides a 'slight decline' in Communications adjusted EBITDA margin (src 1). Chain evidence: MasTec Communications EBITDA margin 8.2% vs 9.9% (-170bp) and 18-month Communications backlog $5,501M -> $5,461M QoQ (src 9); Verizon's 2026 guide is a capex decrease of $0.5-1bn including Frontier (src 16). Arithmetic: a 50bp Communications margin shortfall on ~$6.5B FY28 Communications revenue x (1 - 25% tax, assumed) / 30.16M shares = $0.81 = 3.9% of $20.78, rounded to 4%: $20.78 x 0.96 = $19.95.

$19.95 x 1.10 = $21.95. 10% is below FY28 consensus revenue growth (+13.2%, src 3). Supported by multi-year carrier build plans: AT&T >36M fiber locations, 40M by end-2026 and 60M by 2030 (~5M/yr, src 16); Verizon 40-50M passings medium term (src 11); FBA ~60M first-time passings remaining (src 10); DY backlog $12.24B (src 1). Held at 10% rather than consensus-like growth because Verizon is cutting capex (src 16).

FY28 ends late Jan-2028 (FY27 ends Jan 30, 2027, src 1), so ~3.7 of the 12 months after 2027-10-09 fall in FY28: 0.31 x $19.95 + 0.69 x $21.95 = $6.18 + $15.15 = $21.33. Replaces round-1 roll-forward ($19.95 x 1.075 = $21.45).

Value: 16.0 x $21.33 = $341. bear.story: Telecom softness spreads. Verizon keeps cutting capex (2026 guide -$0.5-1bn), the SpaceX spectrum push makes carriers defend cash flow, the wireless deferral is not recaptured and wireline slows, and the early-March 2027 FY28 outlook shows Communications declining. The supplier-finance build ($367M) unwinds and FCF turns negative, so net debt rises. NTM EPS resets to ~$16.5 and the stock trades at ~11.5x: 16.5 x 11.5 = ~$190.

base.story: FY27 is delivered ($7.48-7.66B) and the ~$150M wireless deferral lands in FY28. NTM EPS is ~$21 (consensus less the chain haircut), AT&T's fiber ramp toward 60M locations by 2030 offsets Verizon's capex trim, and Building Systems backlog converts. The multiple recovers only partly, to ~14.3x, because leverage (~2.9x) and supplier-finance-flattered cash flow cap re-rating: 21 x 14.3 = ~$300.

bull.story: The $12.2B backlog converts and the FY28 outlook shows Communications growth plus wireless recapture. Hyperscaler capex rises again in 2027 (2026 guides were raised: Alphabet $195-205B, Amazon ~$220B, Meta $130-145B, Microsoft ~$175B), driving long-haul and inside-the-fence fiber and Power Solutions. MasTec Communications stabilises. NTM EPS ~$22.5 at ~19x, MasTec's level: ~$425.

comps_summary.peer_range: 8 peers (MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG, EME, FIX, STRL, IESC). Forward P/E 19.89x (MTZ) to 38.32x (PWR), median 23.29x; telecom core MTZ 19.89x and PRIM 21.12x. Fewer than 10 peers because ROAD (paving), AGX (power-plant EPC) and LMB (small mechanical contractor, outlier-low) are not genuine comparables for a telecom-led specialty contractor; no other listed US specialty contractor has DY's telecom mix. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 16.0x NTM P/E: ~20% below MTZ (19.89x), ~31% below the 23.29x median, below the peer range, and slightly above DY's current 14.60x. 10.5x EV/EBITDA on FY28E (~ horizon-trailing) adjusted EBITDA: ~30% below MTZ's 15.12x trailing and below DY's own 11.61x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: A discount to the closest peer, MasTec, should persist through the horizon for verified structural reasons. (1) Leverage: DY net debt/TTM EBITDA is ~2.90x ($2.70B / $931.98M, src 4) vs MTZ ~2.23x ($2.92B / $1.31B, src 17). Notional net debt is $2,502.6M and rose $201M in Q2 (src 5). (2) Cash quality: supplier-finance obligations went from $0 to $367.4M in a year (src 6), the FY26 AP increase of $223.2M provided FY26 operating cash flow (src 7), and H1 FY27 FCF was -$54.2M (src 5). Reported FCF overstates what is repeatable. (3) Concentration: AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4% and Lumen 5.3% = 35.8% of Q2 revenue (src 2), and Verizon is cutting 2026 capex by $0.5-1bn (src 16). (4) The telecom end market is soft across the chain: MasTec Communications margin -170bp (src 9) and DY's own Communications margin outlook turned to 'slight decline' (src 1). I do not go further below (e.g. DY's 14.6x) because FY28 EPS growth (+21.9%) is in line with the peer set and Building Systems (24.5% Q2 margin, data-center electrical in Greater DC/MD/VA) is the kind of business EME and FIX are valued at 23-32x for. Amortization is not used as a discount reason, since DY's adjusted EPS excludes amortization on the same basis as consensus. [Citation gate 2026-10-12] Leverage from filings: lease-inclusive net debt / company-adjusted TTM EBITDA 2.82x for DY ($2,708.3M / $959.8M) vs 2.12x for MTZ ($2,919.8M / $1,379.5M); 2.58x vs 1.76x ex leases.

thesis_break_reason: $190 is ~29% below the current price, ~9.1x FY28 consensus EPS ($20.78) and ~28% below the $263.36 52-week low. A trade there would mean an earnings reset to NTM EPS in the mid-teens, not ordinary 52%-vol noise. Likely causes: the early-March 2027 FY28 outlook shows Communications declining even after the ~$150M wireless recapture; AT&T or Verizon (30.5% of Q2 revenue) cut programs, where Verizon is already lowering capex and the SpaceX spectrum push pressures carrier budgets; MasTec-style Communications margin erosion turns into volume loss; or the $367M supplier-finance build reverses and drives FCF and net debt the wrong way.

reasoning: Round 2 update. Supervisor findings I verified at source: notional net debt $2,502.6M (Q2 deck); supplier-finance obligations $0 -> $226.4M -> $349.4M -> $367.4M (SEC XBRL); FY26 OCF $642.5M with a $223.2M AP increase (10-K) against FY26 FCF $435.3M (Q4 release); StockAnalysis EV $10.82B uses $3.05B total debt including ~$0.23B leases; DY net debt/TTM EBITDA 2.90x vs MTZ 2.23x. Consequences: horizon net debt raised from $2.18B to $2.30B notional, plus $0.23B leases for the EV leg; EV/EBITDA multiple trimmed from 11x to 10.5x; P/E put on a calendar-weighted NTM basis ($21.33 vs $21.45); peer set cut to 8 genuine comparables (median 23.29x), with the 16x discount argued against MTZ on verified leverage, cash quality and concentration. Fair value $352 -> $338. New industry evidence: Verizon's 2026 capex guide is down $0.5-1bn while AT&T's rises toward 60M fiber locations by 2030 (Omdia); the Oct 9 SpaceX-Grain spectrum deal hit carrier stocks 5.5-7.4% and lifted towers (Reuters), which is mixed for DY. Dropped: the unverified 'new buyback' catalyst and the press recaps of the August sell-off. Where I differ from the supervisor: I use 10.5x on FY28E EBITDA (about the horizon's trailing EBITDA) rather than 10x NTM, and I assume no buybacks in horizon net debt ($2.30B vs its $2.35B), since none is in the Q2 release. Distribution: three-scenario lognormal mixture (bear $190/30% sd 0.30; base $300/45% sd 0.22; bull $425/25% sd 0.25), median ~$293, mean ~$308, with tails widened toward the 52% realized vol. P(>= $269) = 0.59 (from 0.605): valuation support (14.6x vs a 23.3x median, FY28 consensus $20.78 intact) is offset by verified cash-quality and leverage concerns, chain softness and strong negative momentum. Research limits: sec.gov refused a scripted fetch with a generic User-Agent, so filings were read with WebFetch; StockAnalysis gates FY29 consensus, so FY29 growth is my judgment; peer forward EV/EBITDA is unavailable, so trailing figures are shown.
